Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29 09:37 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Redwood CSM); Priya Patel (Head of ML, Luna), Daniel Kim (CTO), Alex Rivera (Infrastructure), Grace O'Neil (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on: committed capacity upsell (3x dedicated pool), adding EU-West region for data residency and latency, clarifying KMS/HSM integration and audit logs, and timeline for contract extension/PO. Agreed to run benchmarks in EU-West and to circulate updated pricing and SOC2/KMS docs.

Topics: capacity upgrade, additional regions (EU-West), data residency, SOC2/KMS, benchmarks, contract/PO timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I know it's holiday-ish so we'll keep this tight. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya: Yep, Priya here. Hi, uh, Daniel and Alex are on as well - Grace is here for procurement.
[00:17] Daniel: Morning.
[00:18] Alex: Hey.
[00:21] Sofia: Great. Marco, you want to kick off with the technical recap?
[00:25] Marco: Sure. So from our notes the main asks were: 1) committed dedicated capacity - they're looking at roughly 3x their current pool for peak batch jobs, 2) add EU-West region for production traffic and data residency, and 3) KMS / audit log details for compliance. I'm going to talk through latency expectations and what the dedicated pool buys you.
[00:42] Priya: Quick clarification - by "3x" we mean three times the current concurrent inference slots, mostly for end-of-day reconciliation and fraud scoring spikes. Not necessarily sustained 24/7.
[00:52] Marco: Yeah, that's what we heard. The committed pool gives you guaranteed throughput with bursting on top if you need it but the price changes slightly.
[01:05] Alex: On the region side, can Redwood add an EU-West 1 region as prod? Right now we have EU on the roadmap but need it sooner because of a new partner in Ireland.
[01:17] Marco: We can. For Dedicated, we can spin up a regional pool - it just affects the commit and pricing, and there are some networking pre-reqs for VPC peering. Also, note that private deployments have a different onboarding time, that was an ask earlier about "on-prem" but sounds like VPC peering is the route.
[01:38] Daniel: When you say VPC peering, you mean the usual VPC peering with route tables? We run strict egress rules.
[01:45] Marco: Yep, it's standard VPC peering, plus we can arrange for IP allow lists and private link if you prefer. We'll share a network checklist.
[01:53] Priya: On security, can you confirm the KMS/HSM flow? We need to show auditors how keys are used and whether Redwood can bring-your-own-key.
[02:04] Marco: Yes - BYOK supported for Dedicated and Private. We support partner KMS and HSMs; I'll send the KMS integration doc. Important note: some cloud regions have restrictions on HSM access, we'll call that out for EU-West.
[02:18] Priya: Great. Also retention - audit logs retention for inference requests, how long can we keep them and can we turn off retention for specific routes?
[02:28] Leah (CSM): We have per-route retention controls. You can set retention to zero for PII routes; default is 90 days for hosted, but Dedicated/Private policies can be customized in the contract.
[02:38] Grace: From procurement - what's the proposed extension term and billing cadence? We typically do annual PO.
[02:45] Sofia: We proposed 12-month renewal with a committed pool add-on. Pricing example: base renewal plus Dedicated 3x pool add-on for EU-West. We can offer monthly invoicing if needed but PO terms need to be in contract. I'll circulate a term sheet.
[02:58] Grace: Ok please include sample SLA language, uptime target.
[03:03] Marco: SLA for Dedicated is SLA-backed latency and uptime - we'll send the standard SLA doc. Also in practice, dedicated reduces tail latency variance, which is helpful for your fraud scoring spikes.
[03:17] Daniel: Speaking of latency, can we do a quick benchmark? If we add EU-West pool, we want to see p99 tail<120ms for short chat-like calls and 200-300ms for longer sequences.
[03:29] Marco: Yeah we can spin up a test pool and run a load test. Alex, can you provide IP ranges and a small sample dataset for your typical sequences? We'll run tests and share metrics.
[03:40] Alex: I can. We'll anonymize data but keep distribution similar. Also, curious about KV cache behavior across regions - if we have split traffic between US and EU, will cold starts for the KV cache hurt us?
[03:53] Marco: Good question. KV cache is per-serving pool. If you split traffic, you either replicate prefix caches or accept cold starts. For high locality, route EU traffic to EU pool and you'll get local KV caches and better latency. There's some overhead if you route a lot of traffic cross-region.
[04:10] Priya: Any cost guidance on cache replication?
[04:13] Marco: Replicating large KV caches increases storage and sync cost; usually customers with strict residency do regional caches and accept higher infra cost. We'll include numbers in the pricing spreadsheet.
[04:24] Priya: Also backups - do we need to handle model weights residency? Model artifacts are fine in US, but inference logs must stay in EU.
[04:33] Marco: We can serve model weights from a central S3, but inference logs can be routed and stored only in EU. We'll note that in configuration.
[04:42] Grace: From legal: any change to termination clauses for committed capacity? We prefer some flexibility if traffic drops.
[04:49] Sofia: We can offer a graduated ramp-down with notice - typical enterprise terms allow a partial credit for early reduction after a notice period. We'll flag that to legal.
[04:59] Daniel: One last question - competitor ask: we've been kicked on pricing vs Anthropic and our in-house infra team also looked at renting GPUs. What makes Redwood the right choice for us?
[05:11] Sofia: Two things - predictable unit economics with our optimize toolkit (batching, quant profiles), and less ops overhead - also rollouts and tracing make it easier to detect quality regressions. Marco can share a cost comparison sheet.
[05:25] Marco: Yup, cost + operational velocity; we also have built-in quality monitoring tied to prompt sets so you don't regress model outputs during a rollout.
[05:35] Priya: That's helpful.
[05:37] Sofia: Ok quick recap of next steps: Marco will share SOC2/KMS docs and a sample network checklist by end of week, Sofia to send pricing and term sheet for 12-month renewal plus Dedicated 3x EU-West add-on, Alex to provide IP ranges and sample sequences, Grace to send procurement PO cadence. We'll schedule the EU run benchmark for early Jan.
[05:58] Leah: I'll create the follow-up calendar invite and include the runbook template.
[06:03] Grace: Thanks all.
[06:05] Sofia: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (VPC -> V P C, KMS -> K M S), some names slightly off in auto transcript. Natural pauses and crosstalk present.
